NEW DELHI: The Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) on Friday announced that 17 metro stations across the national capital will remain closed for entry and exit from 7.30am on Friday until further instructions, citing "security reasons".The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central Delhi amid the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the DMRC said interchange facilities will remain available at Rajiv Chowk, Mandi House and Central Secretariat despite the closures.The decision comes a day after the DMRC shut 17 stations on Thursday, following the closure of 16 stations on Wednesday, when hundreds of office-goers, students and other commuters were stranded during the morning rush hour.Entry gates at Mandi House, Rajiv Chowk and Central Secretariat were reopened later on Thursday night.The repeated closures come amid heightened security across central Delhi following the July 20 'Sansad Chalo' march, which witnessed clashes between protesters and police near Parliament.Since then, authorities have maintained heavy security deployment around Jantar Mantar, Parliament and adjoining areas, with prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) remaining in force across the New Delhi district.The CJP has continued its sit-in at Jantar Mantar, demanding the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET paper leak and broader reforms in the examination system.The DMRC has advised commuters to plan their journeys accordingly, adding that normal operations at the affected stations will resume only after further instructions.
Article Summary: 17 Delhi Metro stations will remain closed for entry and exit from 7.30am on Friday until further instructions, citing "security reasons" The latest advisory marks the third consecutive day of metro disruptions in central Delhi amid the ongoing Cockroach Janta Party (CJP)-led protest at Jantar Mantar.

Article Title: Andhra Pradesh and Telangana school holiday today? How students can verify if institutions remain open safely
Article Text:
No official school holiday declared in Andhra Pradesh or Telangana today; students advised to verify institution status

Private institutions announce local closures

How to check whether your school or college is open

Verify local conditions before travelling

No statewide government holiday has been declared for schools or colleges in Andhra Pradesh or Telangana on July 24, 2026. Educational institutions in both states are officially expected to function as usual. However, several private schools, colleges and select higher education institutions have independently suspended classes or postponed examinations following a bandh call by student organisations.The disruption follows a state-wide protest announced by student unions, including SFI, NSUI, PDSU and AISF, over alleged irregularities and the reported paper leak in the NEET examination. As a result, the operational status of institutions varies across districts, making it necessary for students and parents to confirm whether their respective campuses are functioning before travelling.In Telangana, the state government has not issued an official holiday notification for educational institutions. Despite this, several private schools and colleges in Hyderabad and other districts informed parents late on Thursday night that classes would remain suspended for the day. Osmania University has also postponed examinations that were scheduled for July 24, 2026.In Andhra Pradesh, the state government has maintained that schools should continue regular academic activities. However, student organisations have called for widespread participation in the bandh, prompting several private educational institutions in different districts to suspend classes independently.Students and parents should first check official communication channels used by their school or college, including WhatsApp groups, SMS alerts, email notifications and institution mobile applications, as many managements circulated closure notices late on Thursday.If no official message has been received, parents are advised to contact the school or college administration directly by telephone before leaving home. Institutions can confirm whether classes, examinations or transport services are operating as scheduled.Students attending universities should also monitor official notices issued by their institution, particularly if examinations or practical sessions were scheduled for the day.Parents and students should also follow updates from local authorities and regional news outlets for information on protest gatherings, traffic diversions or public transport disruptions in their area. Since closures have been decided by individual institutions rather than through a government order, attendance schedules may differ between schools and colleges within the same district.
Article Summary: No statewide government holiday declared for schools or colleges in Andhra Pradesh or Telangana on July 24, 2026. Several private schools, colleges and select higher education institutions have independently suspended classes or postponed examinations. The disruption follows a state-wide protest announced by student unions.

Article Title: Won’t forget Indian military’s rescue of 12 Chinese crew members after ship fire: China's defence attache
Article Text:
Defence Attache to India, Rear Admiral You Jian thanked Indian military for rescuing 12 Chinese crew members last year

NEW DELHI: China’s newly appointed Defence Attache to India, Rear Admiral You Jian, has thanked the Indian military for rescuing 12 Chinese crew members from a cargo ship that caught fire last year, saying Beijing “will not forget” the operation."We will not forget that, last June, the Indian Military rescued 12 Chinese crew members from a cargo ship that caught fire and exploded off the coast of Kerala," You said while speaking at a reception marking the 99th anniversary of the founding of the Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA). The Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard had jointly carried out the rescue operation to save the lives of the Chinese crew.A senior Chinese military officer lauding the effort of the Indian military is aimed at improving the relations between the two countries. New Delhi and Beijing have engaged in multiple constructive and forward-looking discussions towards gradual normalisation after the 2020 LAC faceoff.The Chinese defence attache also called for closer communication and cooperation between the armed forces of the two countries. He also highlighted the role played by the armed forces of both countries in United Nations peacekeeping operations. “We need to remember that both the Chinese and Indian armed forces have made outstanding contributions and great sacrifices in UN peacekeeping operations.We have always believed that the common interests between our two countries far outweigh our differences,” You said.On deepening military engagement, he said, “We are willing to work with the Indian side to maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels, enhance mutual trust and promote cooperation through dialogue, and contribute to the well-being of the peoples of China and India.”
Article Summary: China’s newly appointed Defence Attache to India, Rear Admiral You Jian, has thanked the Indian military for rescuing 12 Chinese crew members from a cargo ship that caught fire last year. The Indian Navy and the Indian Coast Guard had jointly carried out the rescue operation to save the lives of the Chinese crew.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi's protest outside PM house ‘insincere’: Sonam Wangchuk’s wife
Article Text:
Gitanjali J Angmo, activist Sonam Wangchuk’swife, called “insincere” the flash protest led by CongressMP Rahul Gandhi

NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk 's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo, has criticised the flash protest led by Congress neta Rahul Gandhi near PM Narendra Modi's residence on July 21 as "insincere"."The protest outside the PM's house lacked sincerity. It would have been more sincere if it had been done by joining hands at Jantar Mantar. So, the public cannot be fooled anymore. This is an awakened India," Angmo told India Today in an interview."The awakened India movement has shown us and shown every political functionary that they now have to walk the talk. They cannot gaslight or be insincere anymore. They have to be sincere, otherwise, they will be thrown out by this young generation that has understood what they have to do and what they have to stand for..."Her remarks came two days after Rahul and other senior netas staged a sit-in near the PM's residence at 7 Lok Kalyan Marg over the crackdown on student protesters during their march towards Parliament on July 20. Taking on BJP, Angmo said, "I am very ashamed to say that BJP calls itself a Hindu nationalist party. Because there is nothing about them that is Hindu, and there's nothing about them that is nationalistic," she was quoted as saying."Everybody was there for a cause. That was a demonstration of what Hinduism is. Obstruction of justice, obstruction of freedom, obstruction of protest and terming youths as anti-nationals - this is not nationalism," she said.In an X post, Angmo, who is the co-founder of Himalayan Institute of Alternatives Ladakh (HIAL), said, "As an educator, I find it deeply painful to watch the image of our students being tarnished on media... The students' protest is taking place peacefully at Jantar Mantar. If there are reports of violence elsewhere in Delhi, please do not rush to attribute them to this movement without evidence." She added, "Our children deserve to be protected, not portrayed as villains. Their voices deserve to be heard, not drowned out by narratives that serve vested interests."
Article Summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk's wife, Gitanjali J Angmo, has criticised the flash protest led by Congress neta Rahul Gandhi near PM Narendra Modi's residence on July 21. "The protest outside the PM's house lacked sincerity. It would have been more sincere if it had been done by joining hands at Jantar Mantar," she said.

Article Title: MPs ask why govt didn’t inform owners of non-E20 vehicles about mileage loss
Article Text:
MPs questioned why the government did not warn owners of non-E20 vehicles about possible mileage loss.

NEW DELHI: Members of the parliamentary committee on transport Thursday asked top government officials on why no effort was made to inform owners of non-E20 compliant vehicles about potential mileage loss due to use of 20% ethanol blended petrol in these vehicles.TOI has learnt that some members also asked officials whether any economic analysis has been carried out to assess whether E20 fuel has had any gain to individual vehicle owners even as they agreed that the increased ethanol blending in petrol has helped the country to reduce dependence on imported crude.The panel headed by JDU’s Sanjay Jha had called officials from road transport and petroleum ministries, representatives from vehicle testing agencies and oil marketing companies, amid the ongoing controversy over impact of E20 on mileage and engines of old vehicles.Some members asked why there is so much sudden opposition and criticism when govt claims that over 19% ethanol blended fuel has been sold for more than two years.“Some members pointed out that since the controversy has peaked, all departments, vehicle manufacturers, oil companies and test agencies have aligned. They also sought exact mileage loss due to E20 fuel. Road transport ministry officials said mileage loss is between 2 and 6% as opposed to some hearsay claiming to be 25%,” said a person privy to the discussion.One of the participants said that officials pointed out two issues that may have triggered the fresh row were — the BIS notification for higher blended ethanol E22, E25 and E30, and sale of adulterated fuels.
Article Summary: MPs questioned why the government did not warn owners of non-E20 vehicles about possible mileage loss. Some members also asked officials whether any economic analysis has been carried out to assess whether E20 fuel has had any gain to individual vehicle owners.

Article Title: 400 Pakistani handles revived from Op Sindoor target NEET protests, being blocked: Delhi Police
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Delhi Police on Thursday said it had identified and blocked more than 400 Pakistani social media handles allegedly spreading misinformation and rumours amid the ongoing protests, urging people not to fall for fake content circulating online.Addressing the media, deputy commissioner of Police (DCP) Sumit Jha said the same social media accounts had also been active during Operation Sindoor and were now attempting to exploit the current situation to provoke people and distract students."We have noticed that some attempts are being made to spread misinformation on social media. So far, more than 400 Pakistani social media handles have been identified, which are taking advantage of this situation and spreading fake content and rumors. They are being blocked. These are the same social media handles which were active during Operation Sindoor as well. Their only aim is to provoke people and especially divert the attention of students. "Jha appealed to the public, particularly students and parents, not to be influenced by unverified posts, edited videos or content shared by anonymous accounts."I appeal to you that for the safety of children, do not get provoked by any fake post, edited videos or any post made by anonymous handle. Fact check any post before sharing it. Do not spread rumors and do not let any anti-social elements control your emotions."He also reiterated that the police respected citizens' right to peaceful protest."Remember that it is your right to hold a peaceful protest and Delhi Police respects this right."
Article Summary: Delhi Police says it has identified and blocked more than 400 Pakistani social media handles allegedly spreading misinformation and rumours. Deputy commissioner of Police Sumit Jha said the same social media accounts had also been active during Operation Sindoor and were now attempting to exploit the current situation to provoke people and distract students.

Article Title: 'In view of possible violence in the country': Sonam Wangchuk ends hunger strike after 26 days; PM Modi 'prays for his health'
Article Text:
Sonam Wangchuk ended his hunger strike after 26 days

NEW DELHI: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday ended his 26-day hunger strike in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, saying the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country.In a post on X, Wangchuk said he broke his fast in the presence of the two Union ministers and senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh Ladakh. He said 65 MPs from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast."This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile, I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," Wangchuk said. PM Modi wished the activist good health. "I urge Sonam ji to follow his routine as per the doctors' advice and regain his old weight as soon as possible. I pray to the Lord that Sonam ji remains healthy," the Prime Minister said.Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party, with whom Wangchuk had aligned with when he started the hunger strike, said, "We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days.Thank you, sir, for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country," said founder Abhijeet Dipke.Wangchuk had been shifted from Delhi's Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital in Gurugram following directions from the Delhi High Court.Meanwhile, PM Modi also released a video message addressing students protesting over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. Calling the issue "very painful" for lakhs of students and their families, the Prime Minister said the Union Cabinet would consider stricter measures against paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishment for offenders, with the government aiming to introduce the legislation in Parliament during the ongoing Monsoon Session. He also said the government's immediate priority after the alleged leak was to ensure that nearly 22 lakh students did not lose an academic year by conducting the re-examination at the earliest.On the other hand, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called to continue nationwide "peaceful protests" demanding the resignation of union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak. "The Cockroach Janta Party’s peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns," said Dipke in the statement about Wangchuk ending his hunger strike.The Centre had reiterated its willingness to hold talks with student representatives. Union minister Jitendra Singh said the government had sent four formal proposals for discussions and that he and Union Health Minister JP Nadda would be present during the talks.However, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the party had not received any communication from the government and remained ready for talks at Jantar Mantar or a neutral venue such as the Constitution Club of India.Read more: 'More strict actions to come against paper leaks' - PM Modi announces new Bill push
Article Summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday ended his 26-day hunger strike. He said the decision followed prolonged negotiations and was taken to avoid any possibility of violence in the country. PM Modi wished the activist good health. Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called to continue nationwide "peaceful protests"

Article Title: 2,500 detained, homes of 2 LeT terrorists razed in Kashmir after cop killing
Article Text:
2 LeT terrorists arrested

SRINAGAR: Security forces demolished family homes of two “wanted” Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists and detained more than 2,500 people for questioning across Kashmir overnight in a sweeping crackdown following Wednesday’s fatal shooting of a J&K police head constable on duty in Lal Chowk market in Anantnag town.Officials said Thursday forces used controlled explosives to demolish the house where Adil Ahmad Thoker’s family lives in Guri village of Anantnag district. It was the second time the house was blown up after a similar demolition following the Pahalgam terrorist attack that killed 26 people on April 22, 2025.Forces also demolished the house of Haroon Rashid Ganaie’s family at Hassanpora Tawella in Bijbehara. Teams reached both villages around 3am and asked occupants to leave before detonating explosives. Thoker and Ganaie have been associated with LeT since 2018.Police said those detained were suspected “overground workers” accused of providing logistics, shelter, cash, transport, communications and other support to terrorists. About 700 were detained in Srinagar district, 178 in Baramulla, 200 in Budgam, 100 in Ganderbal, and several hundred more in Anantnag, Shopian and Kulgam.A police officer said the operation aimed to identify and dismantle networks providing logistical, financial, communication, transport and shelter support to terrorist organisations.LG Manoj Sinha chaired a security review Thursday and directed officials to remain “highly vigilant” and neutralise emerging threats. He also reviewed arrangements for Amarnath Yatra, suspended since July 19 because of heavy rain. More than 391,000 have visited the cave shrine in Anantnag district in the first 20 days of the annual pilgrimage.Officials said the manhunt continues for the lone terrorist who murdered 45-year-old head constable Ashiq Hussain Qureshi, a father of three from Lalpora village in central Kashmir’s Budgam.CM Omar Abdullah criticised the demolitions and detentions, calling the police action counter-productive. “People are angry that a police head constable has been killed so brutally. But when the number of arrests rises from hundreds to 2,000 or 2,500, that public anger risks being redirected against us,” he said. “So, demolishing houses or making thousands of arrests will not help improve the situation.”Peoples Conference chairman Sajad Lone and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti called the detentions “mass arrests”, saying they “look more like community punishment”.
Article Summary: Security forces demolish homes of two 'wanted' Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorists. More than 2,500 people detained for questioning across Kashmir overnight. Crackdown follows fatal shooting of a J&K police head constable on duty.

Article Title: SC issues notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla against approval of Sena (UBT) MPs' merger with Shinde faction
Article Text:
SC issues notice to Om Birla (ANI images)

Moved to SC earlier

Merger alters Lok Sabha numbers

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday issued notices to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Lok Sabha Secretary and six rebel Shiv Sena MPs on a plea filed by the Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray (UBT) faction challenging the Speaker's decision to recognise the merger of the six MPs with the Eknath Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The top court has further posted the matter for hearing after two weeks.The plea was filed by UBT MP Arvind Ganpat Sawant against the Speaker's decision, which was approved ahead of the Monsoon Session of Parliament. A bench comprising Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe issued notice to the respondents while refusing to stay the Speaker's order at this stage.The Shiv Sena (UBT) on Tuesday approached the Supreme Court challenging Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's decision to approve the merger of its six MPs with the Shiv Sena led by Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde.Senior advocate Devadatt Kamat, appearing for the Uddhav Thackeray-led party, mentioned the matter before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M. Pancholi, seeking an urgent hearing on Wednesday.Ahead of the Monsoon Session, Speaker Om Birla approved the merger of six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs with the Shinde-led Shiv Sena.The MPs are Sanjay Deshmukh (Yavatmal), Sanjay Jadhav (Parbhani), Sanjay Dina Patil (Mumbai North East), Nagesh Patil-Ashtikar (Hingoli), Omprakash Rajenimbalkar (Dharashiv) and Bhausaheb Wakchaure (Shirdi).With the merger, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Shiv Sena's strength in the Lok Sabha has come down to three MPs, while the Shinde-led Shiv Sena's tally has increased to 13 MPs, making it the third-largest constituent of the NDA after the BJP and the Telugu Desam Party (TDP).Reacting to the development, Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde said the six MPs joined his party to secure development for their constituencies and not for "personal gains".
Article Summary: Supreme Court issues notices to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, the Lok Sabha Secretary and six rebel Shiv Sena MPs. Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray (UBT) faction challenging Speaker's decision to recognise the merger of the six MPs with the Eknath Shinde-led ShivSena.

Article Title: NIA arrests absconding PFI district chief in Kerala's Sreenivasan murder case
Article Text:
NIA arrested a key absconder in Kerala’s Sreenivasan murder case

NEW DELHI: National Investigation Agency (NIA) ion Thursday arrested a key absconder in Kerala’s Sreenivasan murder case, linked with the banned Popular Front of India (PFI) terrorist organisation.Muhammadali K.P, the PFI Palakkad district president, was taken into custody on Thursday morning at the IGI Airport, New Delhi, on his arrival from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where he had been hiding for the past four years. With this, the total number of accused arrested in the case now stands at 67.Among the 65 accused chargesheeted so far in the case, Muhammadali K.P is facing charges under relevant sections of IPC and UA (P) Act.Hailing from Palakkad district in Kerala, the wanted accused was a prominent perpetrator of the murder conspiracy and had also harboured the assailants involved in the brutal killing of Sreenivasan on April 16, 2022. NIA had declared a reward of Rs 3 lakh for information leading to his arrest and an Interpol Red Notice was also issued against him.Sreenivasan was killed by PFI cadres in pursuance of the PFI conspiracy to unleash terror with the nefarious agenda of establishing Islamic Rule in India by 2047. NIA, which had registered the case in September 2022, found during investigation that the accused involved in the case had conspired to create a communal divide through violent extremism and Jihad in the country.Investigations had further revealed that PFI was operating through various Wings and units established for the said purpose, and was using its offices, campuses, facilities and infrastructure to impart arms training to selected cadres in the guise of physical education, yoga training etc through its physical education Wing. The reporters wing was tasked with collecting information about prospective targets, while the actual terror acts were executed by the ‘service teams’ who trained in handling of weapons.
Article Summary: National Investigation Agency (NIA) ion Thursday arrested a key absconder in Kerala’s Sreenivasan murder case. Muhammadali K.P, the PFI Palakkad district president, was taken into custody on Thursday morning at the IGI Airport, New Delhi. With this, the total number of accused arrested in the case now stands at 67.

Article Title: 2 new secretaries in education ministry, Vineet Joshi moved to panchayati raj
Article Text:
Joshi moved to panchayati raj

NEW DELHI: Amid ongoing protests over NEET-UG paper leak issue, govt Thursday named new secretaries for higher and school education departments, with incumbent Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department.While animal husbandry secretary Naresh Pal Gangwar was appointed the new secretary for higher education, TK Anil Kumar will be the new school education secretary. The changes mark an overhaul of sorts in education ministry bureaucracy, as Abhishek Singh was earlier named head of the National Testing Agency , which conducts NEET, CUET and other exams.In early June, CBSE chief Rahul Singh and secretary Himanshu Gupta were transferred out of the National Testing Agency after a controversy over on-screen marking.The secretary-level appointments included 13 new department heads, including a bifurcation of ministry of housing and urban affairs. MoHUA secretary K Srinivas has been shifted to development of north eastern region (DoNER) ministry. D Thara, from Gujarat cadre, has been appointed secretary of the just-created department of capital development, while her batchmate Satendra Singh from Jharkhand will lead the department of urban development.The changes in education ministry are significant as govt has said demand for removal of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan is not under consideration, but steps will be taken to address concerns. The appointments committee of cabinet also desginated Chandra Bhushan Kumar as new labour secretary, while Keshav Chandra will be the new mines secretary. Odisha cadre IAS officer SK Lohani has been designated as animal husbandry secretary.
Article Summary: Vineet Joshi, who had charge of both, moved to low-profile panchayati raj department. The changes mark an overhaul of sorts in education ministry bureaucracy. Abhishek Singh was earlier named head of the National Testing Agency.

Article Title: 'More strict actions to come against paper leaks': PM Modi announces new Bill push in video message
Article Text:
Prime Minister assures students that strict action will be taken against paper leaks on Friday

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday announced that government will bring in more strict actions against paper leaks. In a late night video message, PM Modi said that the Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures on Friday and the government will try to get the Bill passed in Parliament next week.He assured that the Centre will bring in stricter measures to curb examination paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishments for offenders.His message comes amid massive nationwide protests against alleged irregularities in the NEET UG examination. "I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians.""Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.Further talking about the bill on fast track courts he added, "On the 19th July, the results were declared. I directed the departments today to establish a fast-track court. The departments presented me with the resolution late at night. This resolution, along with the provision for a fast-track court and harsh punishment, will be discussed in the cabinet tomorrow. After the suggestions of cabinet colleagues, it will be finalised, and since the second week of Parliament is starting from Monday, efforts will be made to get that bill passed in the House as soon as possible. "This after PM's remarks, at the NDA parliamentary party meeting on Tuesday, saying that the govt is working to make the exam system “foolproof”.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi assures students that strict action will be taken against paper leaks on Friday. Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures on Friday and the government will try to get the Bill passed in Parliament next week. His message comes amid massive nationwide protests against alleged irregularities in the NEET UG examination.

Article Title: SC laments vanishing of joint family system
Article Text:
SC expressed concern about the vanishing of the joint family system

Expressing concern about the vanishing of the joint family system and parents in nuclear families not spending quality time with their kids and instead handing over gadgets to keep them busy, Supreme Court Thursday said that it would lead to "disaster" as the new generation would be unaware of family bonding and relationships.While analysing the reasons behind recent incidents of people killing spouses, including the case of Sonam Raghuvanshi, a bench of Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale said that it was a reflection of changing society. It said that the present generation is more intelligent and informative, but it does not know how to deal with pressure. The court said that it is unfortunate that people nowadays rely on WhatsApp-circulated messages and treat them as knowledge. Agreeing with the court's concern, solicitor general Tushar Mehta said that it has become a social problem and trust in human relationships is diminishing and there is a lack of tolerance.Justice Sundresh said that he was recently in a restaurant and he saw that a family gave a phone to a kid in order to keep him busy while they were having food. "If parents are replaced by gadgets, then it is a disaster. It is going to happen more in future. Joint family is an asset, and people don't understand it. Happiness does not come with material possession but by human bonding and relationship. We are becoming like machines," he said.
Article Summary: Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale said that the present generation is more intelligent and informative, but it does not know how to deal with pressure. The court said that it is unfortunate that people nowadays rely on WhatsApp- circulated messages and treat them as knowledge.

Article Title: Road crashes killed a record 1.8 lakh in 2025; 502 people daily
Article Text:
Road crashes claimed a little over 1.8 lakh lives in 2025

Death tol lrises

Road crashes claimed a little over 1.8 lakh lives in 2025, translating into 502 deaths per day, which is the maximum since govt started collating data. While the highest increase in such fatalities was reported in Uttar Pradesh -- from 24,118 in 2024 to 27,550 last year -- Punjab saw a major dip in road deaths -- from 4,759 in 2024 to 3,062 last year.Data that the road transport ministry provided to Lok Sabha on Thursday show that road crashes shot up by 5.3% to over 5.1 lakh in 2025 and fatalities increased by 3.5%. Ministry’s written reply indicates that 18 states and UTs saw a rise in road deaths in 2025 while 17 others reported a decline. Significantly, Lakshadweep has not reported any road death in the past two years.Ministry said data for West Bengal, which reported fewer number of fatalities in road crashes, have been taken from eDAR records as of Jan 2, 2026, while in the case of all others, data have been taken from eDAR records as of July 22. The e-Detailed Accident Report (eDAR) is a digital central accident database management system designed to analyse causes of crashes and devise safety measures. Officials said the overall number of fatalities may increase when the data for West Bengal is updated.Experts say the rise in road deaths despite efforts of govt to bring them down indicates that the current strategies have not proven that effective, even in states like Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh and Assam where non-profit organisations in the sector have collaborated with local govts.On Wednesday, the ministry had informed Rajya Sabha that 6,358 “black corridors” on the National Highway (NH) network were identified during 2023-25, which recorded 37,164 deaths. The maximum such black corridors were in Tamil Nadu (958), followed by UP (671) and Karnataka (607). Among districts, Viluppuram in Tamil Nadu had a maximum of 70 such corridors.As per ministry, unlike isolated black spots, these corridors are continuous stretches of NH that have recorded a higher number of road crashes that led to fatalities and grievous injuries. The identification is expected to help the authorities prioritise engineering interventions and improve road safety outcomes, officials said.
Article Summary: Road crashes claimed a little over 1.8 lakh lives in 2025, translating into 502 deaths per day. The highest increase in such fatalities was reported in Uttar Pradesh. Punjab saw a major dip in road deaths -- from 4,759 in 2024 to 3,062 last year.

Article Title: Fast-track courts, bill to tackle leaks: PM Modi
Article Text:
PM Modi shared a late night video message

NEW DELHI: PM Modi late Thursday announced that the Union Cabinet will on Friday discuss a bill to further strengthen the anti-cheating law to ensure stricter punishment to offenders.Hours after ordering the establishment of fast-track courts, in a recorded message posted on social media at midnight, PM said that based on the discussion a bill will be moved on Monday, when the second week of the current Parliament session begins, and govt will seek its passage at the earliest."Fast-track courts and strict punishment will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow and it will be given final shape after the discussion," Modi said, while underlining that govt has been working on addressing the concerns related to medical entrance exams paper leak over the last two and a half months. He said that govt had so far focused on ensuring that students did not lose a year and decided to conduct exams for 22 lakh students, using "all its might", with results also declared.PM Modi's message through the unusual mode came minutes after govt replaced the education secretary amid the ongoing protests against the NEET paper leak.Over the last two days, officials said, PMO has been engaged with the education ministry over the NEET exam, retest and K Radhakrishnan committee on NTA reforms, with over two dozen queries flowing from Seva Teerth.I know a paper leak is not an ordinary incident, it is very painful for lakhs of students and their parents... The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our first and foremost responsibility was to ensure that the NEET aspirants did not lose an academic year. We used all resources to ensure that the re-exam was held in record time and results are out and lakhs of students are also celebrating," he said in the video message on X.The PM said more needed to be done, hinting the bill wo-uld be a step in that direction."Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! Those who try to harm (it) will not be spared," he said in a post on X.
Article Summary: PM Modi shared a late night video message on social media. He said fast-track courts and strict punishment will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow. Modi's message came minutes after govt replaced the education secretary amid the ongoing protests against the NEET paper leak.

Article Title: India invites Bangladesh PM to Brics Summit
Article Text:
India invites Bangladesh PM

DHAKA/NEW DELHI: As part of Delhi's broader approach to enhancing global collaboration and cooperation, India has invited PM Tarique Rahman to attend the 18th Brics Summit, which will focus on global cooperation, trade, and sustainable development. India will host the summit in New Delhi on September 12-13.Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam said Thursday that the ministry had received the invitation from the Indian side and forwarded it to the Prime Minister's Office, without elaborating further.PM Narendra Modi had invited Tarique in Feb too, after he took office. Tarique has so far not appeared inclined to take the political risk of visiting India while former PM Sheikh Hasina remains on Indian soil, amid concerns about a domestic backlash. However, Bangladesh also aspires to become a Brics member and has already received support from China and Russia.Both Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are expected to attend the summit.Tarique recently visited Malaysia and China, and also plans to travel to Japan and the US for the UN General Assembly later this year. An official confirmation of India's invitation is still awaited.India had also invited Bangladesh in 2016, the last time it hosted the Brics summit in person, as a Bimstec member for a Brics outreach session.External affairs minister S Jaishankar on Thursday met Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman on the sidelines of the Asean Regional Forum Foreign Ministers' Meeting in Manila. An official in Dhaka said the two ministers exchanged greetings.Responding to a question on regional instability, Shama Obaed said Bangladesh, as a democratic state with a democratically elected govt, wanted peace and stability in the region. She added that Bangladesh expected India, as a large democratic country, to address its internal issues and move towards a solution.India's Brics chairship is guided by the theme "Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability", reflecting a people-centric approach articulated by Modi at the 2025 Rio Summit. Brics comprises Brazil, China, Egypt, Ethiopia, India, Indonesia, Iran, Russia, Saudi Arabia, South Africa and the UAE as members.The 17th Brics Summit was held on July 6-7, 2025, in Rio de Janeiro in Brazil.
Article Summary: India has invited Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman to attend the 18th Brics Summit. India will host the summit in New Delhi on September 12-13. Bangladesh also aspires to become a Brics member and has already received support from China and Russia.

Article Title: CJP, Centre set for 12:30 pm talks at Constitution Club; Pradhan's resignation among key demand
Article Text:
CJP-Centre meeting to be held today (ANI)

'Peaceful protest will continue'

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) delegation will meet Union ministers at the Constitution Club of India at 12.30 pm on Friday, after the Centre agreed to hold talks at a neutral venue—a key demand raised by the outfit during its ongoing agitation over the NEET row.The meeting comes a day after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, paving the way for formal discussions between the government and the protesters.Confirming the development, CJP chief spokesperson Saurav Das said the organisation welcomed the government's decision to shift the talks to a neutral venue."Our protest will continue; Constitution Club of India chosen as venue for meeting with government ministers, hoping for an open-minded dialogue," Das told reporters on Thursday.CJP spokesperson Vaishnavi Gaur said the delegation would place the same demands it has been raising since the protests began."We will be putting forward our demands, which we have been consistent with from the first day," she said.According to Gaur, the key demands include the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for the families affected by the NEET controversy, and withdrawal of all FIRs registered against what she described as "innocent protesters."Following Wangchuk's decision to end his fast, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke thanked him for what he called an extraordinary act of courage."We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days. Thank you for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country," Dipke wrote in a post on X.Despite Wangchuk ending his fast, the CJP has maintained that its peaceful protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar will continue until its demands, including Pradhan's resignation, are addressed.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) delegation will meet Union ministers at the Constitution Club of India at 12.30 pm on Friday. Meeting comes a day after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike at Medanta Hospital.

Article Title: 'No cases against peaceful protesters': List of govt assurances that ended Sonam Wangchuk's fast
Article Text:
Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight and conveyed the government's assurances.

NEW DELHI: Activist Sonam Wangchuk on Friday ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after receiving assurances from the Centre that key demands raised by students protesting over alleged examination irregularities would be addressed.In a post on X, Wangchuk said the government had assured that there would be a discussion in Parliament on accountability in the examination system, compensation for families of students who died by suicide following the recent NEET paper leak, and no cases against peaceful protesters."END OF HUNGER... BEGINNING OF ACCOUNTABILITY...!" Wangchuk wrote.He added, "Sonam Wangchuk ends his fast after 26 days upon getting assurance from the government and members of parliament of all political parties that the issue of accountability in the failing examination system will be discussed on the floors of the Indian Parliament.""The government also gave assurance that families of suicide victims in the recent NEET examination paper leak will be given adequate compensation and that there will be no cases registered against the peacefully protesting students and youths," he said.Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight and conveyed the government's assurances."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda, Dr Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh, I finally broke my fast after 26 days," Wangchuk wrote.He said 65 Members of Parliament from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast."This was done after long negotiations on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile, I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi welcomed Wangchuk's decision to end the fast. In a post on X, he said, "I urge Sonam ji to follow his daily routine as advised by the doctors and regain his weight as soon as possible.""I pray to the Almighty that Sonam ji remains healthy," the Prime Minister added.The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), which has been leading the protest at Jantar Mantar, welcomed Wangchuk's decision but said its agitation would continue until Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.Wangchuk joined the CJP-led protest on June 28 and began an indefinite hunger strike in support of demands for accountability over alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, reforms to the education system and Pradhan's resignation. During the fast, he lost around 11 kg and continued the protest from Medanta Hospital after being shifted there from Safdarjung Hospital following legal proceedings.
Article Summary: Wangchuk announced the end of his fast after Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh met him at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram around midnight. He said 65 Members of Parliament from different political parties had either visited him or signed letters urging him to end the fast.

Article Title: 'Don't insult students' intelligence': Rahul Gandhi slams PM Modi's midnight video on paper leaks
Article Text: NEW DELHI: Leader of opposition in Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi early Friday attacked Prime Minister Narendra Modi accusing him of sidestepping the demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan 's resignation over the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.Reacting to the Prime Minister's late-night video message on the issue, Rahul said PM Modi should not "insult the intelligence" of students and demanded Pradhan be sacked saying the PM's address failed to raise students' key concerns.In a post on X, Rahul wrote, "Mr Modi, our students are demanding Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. Don't insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight video."Listing his demands, he said:"1. Sack Pradhan.2. Punish those who beat students.3. Apologise."The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after Prime Minister Modi announced that the government would bring a Bill in Parliament next week providing for stringent punishment against those involved in examination paper leaks.In a self-recorded video shared on X late Thursday night, the Prime Minister said the proposed legislation, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stricter penalties, would be discussed by the Union Cabinet on Friday before being introduced in Parliament when the second week of the Monsoon Session begins on Monday."Friends, I know that paper leaks are not an ordinary matter. For lakhs of students and their parents, it is extremely painful," PM Modi said."Our most important responsibility was to ensure that a whole year for the students is not wasted. It was very important to conduct the exams immediately. The government used its full strength to arrange exams for nearly 22 lakh students in the shortest possible time. And just five or six days ago, on the 19th, the results were also announced," he said.The Prime Minister said the government was now moving towards stronger legal action."Today I have issued directions to the departments to set up Fast-Track Courts. The departments worked tirelessly and, late last night, provided me with a draft. This draft, which includes provisions for Fast-Track Courts and stringent punishments, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow," he said.He added that after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, the Bill would be finalised and introduced in Parliament next week."Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi said.The opposition has been demanding Pradhan's resignation and a detailed discussion on the alleged NEET-UG paper leak during the Monsoon Session, with the issue triggering protests both inside Parliament and on the streets.Activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday at Medanta Hospital in the presence of Union ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh, along with senior leaders of the Apex Body of Leh.In a post on X, Wangchuk said he decided to end the fast after prolonged discussions and in view of the possibility of violence."Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr. Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days... This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country," he said."I will explain the conditions in detail in a separate video very soon. Meanwhile urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," he added.Meanwhile, the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) has called for nationwide peaceful protests on Friday, reiterating its demand for Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged examination irregularities.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses Prime Minister Narendra Modi of sidestepping the demand for Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the alleged NEET- UG 2026 paper leak. The leader of oppostion's remarks came hours after PM Modi announced that the government would bring a Bill in Parliament next week providing for stringent punishment.

Article Title: Opposition MPs take out march in solidarity with protesters
Article Text:
Opposition MPs stage protest against govt at Parliament in black clothes

NEW DELHI: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students, two days after they held a dharna outside the PM's residence and were forcibly evacuated by police.The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. From there, they marched to the Gandhi Smriti holding their phone torches. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman, Supriya Sule, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, N K Premachandran, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Arvind Sawant, Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra.Rahul said, "We go to remember the students we lost - the children driven to take their own lives after the NEET paper leak. And we go to stand with the students who lie injured today - beaten for peacefully demanding justice and accountability. India's students are not alone. The entire opposition stands with them and their demands."Congress's P Chidambaram said, "All roads are barricaded, and hundreds of policemen are mobilised to 'secure' the roads of Delhi. What is govt afraid of? Why this sense of panic?" Earlier, Congress rubbished PM Modi's statement assuring the protesting youth. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the students don't need platitudes after govt used pellet guns, shock batons and tear gas on them.
Article Summary: Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students. The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman and Supriya Sule.

Article Title: From fan to critic: Dharmendra Pradhan’s 2023 post resurfaces, reveals changing equations
Article Text:
A 2023 photo of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and Sonam Wangchuk resurfaced recently (Picture credits: X).

Three years are a long time in public life. A 2023 photo of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan with education reformer Sonam Wangchuk and his wife Gitanjali Angmo has acquired a new political life.The March 2023 post, in which Pradhan praised the couple's ideas and commitment to transforming education, resurfaced on social media Thursday as Wangchuk's indefinite hunger strike over examination irregularities entered its 26th day.Wangchuk had responded with similar warmth, thanking Pradhan for being open to innovative ideas and saying the interaction had left them "even more committed to making NEP a reality on the ground". The contrast is sharp.Wangchuk, who had expressed enthusiasm about implementing NEP, is now the most prominent face associated with CJP 's agitation seeking accountability over NEET-UG paper leak and Pradhan's exit.
Article Summary: The March 2023 post, in which Pradhan praised the couple's ideas and commitment to transforming education, resurfaced on social media Thursday. Wangchuk is now the most prominent face associated with CJP's agitation seeking accountability over NEET-UG paper leak andPradhan's exit.

Article Title: IndiGo opposes more say for airport operators in airlines
Article Text:
Rahul Bhatia, promoter and MD of India’s largest carrier IndiGo

NEW DELHI: Rahul Bhatia, promoter and MD of India's largest carrier IndiGo , has opposed the proposed move to allow airport operators in India to own and run airlines too. "There is no global precedent for this. It raises massive conflict-of-interest concerns, and it is unclear how such a move would serve consumers' interests," he said at a post earnings call.Bhatia's Thursday comments come as govt is considering to dilute provisions that disallow operators of Delhi and Mumbai airports to own more than 10% stake in a scheduled airline. While the Adani Group, which runs Mumbai airport, is likely to make the first move by picking up stake in an existing airline or investing in a startup, the GMR Group, which operates Delhi's IGIA, could do so at a subsequent stage.The news has resulted in Interglobe Aviation's shares falling for two consecutive days as investors perceive the airline, which controls two-thirds of the domestic aviation market, to be a loser in case the move goes through.Senior aviation ministry officials said a country with the economic potential of India should have multiple airlines and not just a duopoly with IndiGo and Tata's Air India group.Meanwhile, the Competition Commission of India (CCI) Thursday invited public comments on a commitment proposal by IndiGo in a probe following its last Dec schedule collapse.The airline has proposed temporarily releasing domestic slots at airports. "Post such handover, the airport operator/authority may determine re-allocation of such slots/dates for routes, as deemed fit," the CCI notice says.
Article Summary: Rahul Bhatia, promoter and MD of India's largest carrier IndiGo, has opposed the proposed move to allow airport operators in India to own and run airlines too. "There is no global precedent for this. It raises massive conflict-of-interest concerns, and it is unclear how such a move would serve consumers' interests," he said.

Article Title: CJP's Dipke: Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike Ends, Protest Continues Until Pradhan Resigns
Article Text:
"We are relieved and grateful that Sonam sir has ended his hunger strike after 26 days. Thank you, sir, for your extraordinary courage and sacrifice. By putting your own life on the line, you awakened the conscience of an entire nation. Your life is far too precious to this country,"

"The Cockroach Janta Party's peaceful protest at Jantar Mantar will continue until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns,"

Wangchuk ends 26-day hunger strike

NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Friday expressed relief after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike, while making it clear that its peaceful agitation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar would continue until Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigns.In a post on X, Dipke thanked Wangchuk for what he described as an "extraordinary courage and sacrifice" during the fast.Dipke wrote.However, he further said the end of Wangchuk's fast would not mark the end of the movement.Dipke said.Wangchuk had been on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination and the government's handling of the issue.Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his indefinite hunger strike shortly after midnight at Medanta Hospital in Gurugram in the presence of Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh.He said the decision followed prolonged negotiations with the government and was taken "in view of possible violence in the country.""Just now in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda & Dr Jitendra Singh and the senior leaders of Apex Body of Leh Ladakh I finally broke my fast after 26 days. Earlier 65 Members of Parliament from different political parties had visited or signed letters urging me to break the fast. This was done after a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country. Meanwhile I urge you all to stay very vigilant about not allowing violence of any kind anywhere," Wangchuk posted on X.The CJP protest intensified on July 20 when the 'Sansad Chalo' march towards Parliament ended in clashes between protesters and Delhi Police after demonstrators allegedly attempted to breach barricades. The agitation has since continued at Jantar Mantar demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.The latest security measures, including the temporary suspension of mobile internet services and the early closure of commercial establishments in Connaught Place, come as authorities remain on alert amid concerns over further escalation around the protest site and adjoining parts of Central Delhi.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke expressed relief after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike. Dipke thanked Wangchuk for what he described as an "extraordinary courage and sacrifice" during the fast. Wangchuk had been on an indefinite hunger strike over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination.

Article Title: Low-key Nadda emerges as govt point man in talks with protesters
Article Text:
Nadda emerges as key negotiator from govt's side

NEW DELHI: As the govt's main interlocutor with students protesting under the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) banner, Union health minister JP Nadda has been thrust into the limelight, holding talks with them and visiting the injured in hospitals.This is an interesting turn in Nadda's journey. The former BJP president is not really known for revelling in the spotlight and is more at ease in closed-door political meetings than being in the middle of public attention. That his comments rarely stoke any controversy or ruffle others is being considered an asset when govt is holding talks with a group which is riding the angst of the student community, as any misstep may inflame passions.Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University and grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP, collecting long experience of agitational politics, the second nature of student activism, which makes him the right person for the job.BJP circles are of the view that while being health minister who looked after the treatment of injured protesters put Nadda in a position to connect with CJP, his emergence as a negotiator came as a surprise.It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability. A BJP functionary said one of his strengths was that he was soft-spoken but also knew where to draw the line, a trait that ensures that he could engage with protestors skilfully while ensuring that the govt's views were also put across firmly.He had also met activist Sonam Wangchuk in a private hospital as part of govt's efforts to persuade him to break his hunger strike and engage in talks to end the stir.Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, known for his political savvy and proven track record of successful political outreach, could have been the other choice but for the fact that his resignation is CJP's main demand.With some other leading BJP figures not really a good fit for the job because of their seniority, the task fell on Nadda, now a member of the party's brains trust.
Article Summary: Nadda cut his teeth in students' politics as an ABVP activist in Patna and Himachal University. He grew in the role to head Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha, the youth wing of BJP. It is surmised that the former BJP chief's low-key presence added to his acceptability.

Article Title: No Parliament business, four days into monsoon session
Article Text: NEW DELHI: If the first four days are any indication, monsoon session of Parliament is staring at a washout, with the opposition digging in its heels over its demand for resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, rebuffing invitations from govt for a discussion, reports Subodh Ghildiyal.Amid protests, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha failed to transact business for the fourth consecutive day on Thursday. The stalemate could not be broken despite Speaker Om Birla meeting Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule to defuse the situation. Home minister Amit Shah and parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju also met Birla.Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti in solidarity with the protesting students, two days after they held a dharna outside the PM's residence and were forcibly evacuated by police.The MPs belonging to Congress, SP, TMC, Left parties, RJD, Shiv Sena and others met at Rahul Gandhi's residence. The marchers included Rahul, K C Venugopal, Ramjilal Suman, Supriya Sule, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, N K Premachandran, John Brittas, Sandosh Kumar, Sudhakar Singh, Misa Bharti, Arvind Sawant, Saugata Roy and Mahua Moitra.Rahul said, "We go to remember the students we lost - the children driven to take their own lives after the NEET paper leak.And we go to stand with the students who lie injured today - beaten for peacefully demanding justice and accountability. India's students are not alone. What is govt afraid of? Why this sense of panic?" Earlier, Congress rubbished PM Modi's statement assuring the protesting youth. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the students don't need platitudes after govt used pellet guns, shock batons and tear gas on them.

The stalemate could not be broken despite Speaker Om Birla meeting Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav and Supriya Sule. Opposition MPs took out a 'candlelight march' Thursday to the Gandhi Smriti.

Article Title: SC lifts 2-year-old blanket ban on setting up of industries in Taj zone
Article Text:
SC lifted its two-year-old blanket ban on setting up of industries in Taj Trapezium Zone

NEW DELHI: SC Thursday lifted its two-year-old blanket ban on setting up of industries in Taj Trapezium Zone, a 10,400 sq km area spread over five districts in UP and one in Rajasthan, to open avenues for employment generation. The development comes a few months ahead of UP assembly polls.UP govt, through AG R Venkataramani and ASG Aishwarya Bhati told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that industrial activities, especially when it involves establishment of non-polluting industrial units, cannot be brought to a grinding halt.Seeking modification of SC's Oct 14, 2024 order that barred establishment of any industrial unit in the TTZ area without permission of the court, the AG said, "Keeping in mind aspirations of youth and entrepreneurs, SC should have been a little more flexible when there is a cap on air pollution score of each industry which uses electricity or natural gas as fuel."Senior advocate Aparna Bhat opposed the application, saying the TTZ authority had given arbitrary sanctions for establishment of glass industries which did not meet environmental guidelines. Senior advocate and amicus curiae Liz Mathews suggested to SC that the 410 pending applications for establishment/expansion/relocation of industries in TTZ can be processed by involving green experts from Central Empowered Committee (CEC) and the National Environmental Engineering Research Institute (NEERI).The bench accepted the suggestion after the law officers said the authority is agreeable to any condition for the protection of the environment and the Taj Mahal . It said TTZ authority's Industry Technical Evaluation Committee will involve a domain expert each from CEC and NEERI in the scrutiny of 410 applications."We are giving veto power to the experts. The applications would be entertained by TTZ authority only after the two independent experts from CEC and NEERI concur with the non-pollution character of the industry that is sought to be established," the bench said.It added that in case of dissent from any of the two experts, the proposal would be placed before SC for final adjudication. Even if the experts concurred on setting up of the industry, it would be placed before SC for final clearance, if amicus curiae felt that the matter required judicial scrutiny.The districts falling in the TTZ are Agra, Firozabad, Mathura, Hathras, Etah and Bharatpur.
Article Summary: SC lifted its two-year-old blanket ban on setting up of industries in Taj Trapezium Zone. The 10,400 sq km area is spread over five districts in UP and one in Rajasthan. The development comes a few months ahead of UP assembly polls.

Article Title: Reached out 4 times, says govt; talks at Jantar Mantar or a neutral venue, says CJP
Article Text:
Protests continue at Jantar Mantar

NEW DELHI: Govt made a fresh outreach Thursday to agitating students for talks over the issues being raised by them, emphasising that a solution to the crisis cannot be found without dialogue."I very humbly invite you on behalf of govt to come forward and hold dialogue," Union minister Jitendra Singh, who has joined govt's main emissary and health minister J P Nadda in holding talks with activist Sonam Wangchuk, said, adding the Centre has reached out to Cockroach Janta Party protesters four times since Wednesday afternoon, but has not received any response.CJP has, however, refused to hold another round of talks after meeting Nadda at his residence on July 20, alleging they ended up "wasting" four hours without any outcome. It has insisted on holding the next meeting at Jantar Mantar or at a neutral venue and not at Nadda's residence or office. However, Nadda made it clear the meeting can happen at either of the two places, shrugging off CJP's suggestion.The govt has contested CJP's version of the July 20 meeting. On Thursday, though, the Centre emphasised its keenness to continue with talks to defuse the crisis whenever the protesters want and for as much of length of time as they wish.Union minister Jitendra Singh said, "We are ready to discuss the NEET issue and all other related issues with an open mind." Appealing to protesters, he added, "You will appreciate as much as I do that without talks we cannot find a solution. Without a solution, we cannot lay out further roadmap... Govt does not stand on prestige. Please come forward so that we can find a way out in the larger interest of the youth and the nation at large. "Highlighting PM Modi's announcement of setting up a fast-track court to ensure swift punishment for those involved in paper leaks, he said it attested to govt's commitment to going to any extent to safeguard students' welfare.Education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is a key CJP demand, and govt has so far given little indication that it is even considering the removal of one of its key figures, who has been a member of the Union Cabinet since 2014. Govt has instead conveyed its willingness to engage in talks with protesters over all the issues being raised by them.
Article Summary: CJP has refused to hold another round of talks after meeting Nadda at his residence on July 20. It has insisted on holding the next meeting at Jantar Mantar or at a neutral venue. The govt has contested CJP's version of the July 20 meeting.

Article Title: Pvt investment in space sector crosses $618 million, 17 startups given nod for space activities: Minister Jitendra Singh to RS
Article Text:
India's space sector has witnessed unprecedented momentum with private investment crossing $618.5 million

NEW DELHI: India's space sector has witnessed unprecedented momentum following the landmark reforms, with private investment crossing $618.5 million, 105 authorisations issued to private entities, and a robust regulatory framework being strengthened to safeguard strategic and national security interests while promoting greater private participation, Space, science and technology minister Jitendra Singh informed the Rajya Sabha on Thursday.Replying to an unstarred question in the Rajya Sabha, Singh said cumulative private funding has expanded nearly six-fold in the last few years, rising from $100.5 million in 2021-22 to $348.5 million in 2023-24, before reaching $618.5 million by March 31, 2026, reflecting the growing confidence of domestic and global investors in India's rapidly evolving space ecosystem.Singh informed RS that 17 space startups have so far been authorised by IN-SPACe to undertake space activities, reflecting the emergence of a vibrant startup ecosystem that is increasingly contributing to India's space ambitions. Active space startups have increased from just one in 2014 to over 400 today, while private investment has crossed $600 million.Indian private companies have successfully demonstrated launch and orbital capabilities, placed more than 30 satellites into orbit, and flown nearly 45 payloads through platforms such as the PSLV Orbital Experimental Module (POEM), signalling the growing technological depth and commercial maturity of the country's private space sector.The earth observation public-private partnership has brought together leading Indian companies to develop the country's first privately owned Earth observation satellite constellation with a private investment commitment of around Rs 1,200 crore, demonstrating the growing confidence of industry in India's space reforms.Highlighting the govt's unwavering commitment to ensuring that rapid commercial growth is matched by robust national security safeguards, the minister informed the House that every application for private space activities is evaluated under IN-SPACe's norms, guidelines and procedures with due consideration to strategic, security and national interests before authorisation is granted. He further said IN-SPACe is preparing dedicated safety and security guidelines for space activities in India, in consultation with stakeholders, to further strengthen the country's regulatory architecture as private participation continues to expand.
Article Summary: India's space sector has witnessed unprecedented momentum following landmark reforms. Private investment has crossed $618.5 million, 105 authorisations issued to private entities. 17 space startups have so far been authorised by IN- SPACe to undertake space activities. Indian private companies have successfully demonstrated launch and orbital capabilities.

Article Title: Omar Abdullah to JP Nadda: Right on J&K leak, wrong on facts
Article Text: SRINAGAR: J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah rejected Thursday Union minister JP Nadda ’s claim linking “National Conference (NC) and Congress” to a govt job exam leak in the Union territory, pointing out that the fiasco occurred in 2022 under the lieutenant governor’s (LG) administration when his govt was not in place.Omar indicated that Nadda was correct about the Service Selection Board (SSB) exam leak but got other facts wrong. “It was 2022. Govt wasn’t of NC and Congress. It was a govt headed by LG but thank you for reminding everyone of this failure,” Omar posted.The CM’s response came a day after health minister Nadda accused Omar’s NC and ally Congress of maintaining silence on recruitment-related irregularities, mentioning the “SSB paper leak in J&K, where govt is of Congress and NC”.NC spokesperson and MLA Tanvir Sadiq seized on Nadda’s remarks to accuse “BJP of spreading falsehood” “Such blatant misinformation from a Union minister is both irresponsible and unbecoming,” Sadiq said.The tainted 2022 SSB exams, held for several posts like sub-inspectors and junior engineers, were cancelled over the leak. J&K high court ordered the administration to constitute a high-level probe panel.Posting the HC order, Omar mentioned the court’s observations. “We have no idea what happened to the high-level committee or its report. Perhaps you (Nadda) can share that with us in your next press conference,” Omar wrote.
Article Summary: J&K chief minister Omar Abdullah rejected Thursday Union minister JP Nadda ’s claim linking “National Conference (NC) and Congress’ to a govt job exam leak in the Union territory. “Such blatant misinformation from a Union minister is both irresponsible and unbecoming,” NC spokesperson and MLA Tanvir Sadiq said.

Article Title: Police, SDRF rescue 2 trapped in Tawi river; Army launches relief ops in Reasi, Rajouri
Article Text:
An NDRF personnel evacuates a youth from the middle of the Tawi river

JAMMU: A joint team of J&K Police and SDRF rescued two individuals stranded in the Tawi near Prambli, in Jammu’s Phallian mandal, following a sudden rise in the river’s water level Thursday, even as the Army launched relief and evacuation operations in rain-hit Reasi and Rajouri districts.The duo — Farman Ali (25) from Allora and Farooq Ahmed (28) of Sohanjana — had gone to graze cattle near the river when its water level swelled, leaving them trapped in the middle of the river.After torrential rain triggered landslides and led to the rise in the water level of Arnas river in Reasi, Army troops assisted civilians residing in low-lying areas to move to safer locations, established temporary shelters and provided hot meals, essential supplies, and necessary medical relief in affected areas, defence spokesperson Lt Col Suneel Bartwal said Thursday, adding that a quick reaction team was on standby to respond to any contingency.On receiving information about a civilian suffering from severe dehydration in Panjnara-Peeri area of Rajouri, Army personnel reached the location and conducted a medical assessment before administering first aid, including intravenous fluids, to stabilise the patient’s condition and prevent further deterioration. Following initial treatment, the Army team facilitated the patient’s evacuation for further medical examination and specialised care, Lt Col Bartwal said.A multi-agency operation to trace seven missing people in Murrah, Chang Nallah in Poonch’s Surankote entered the fifth day as round-the-clock searches continued Thursday too. A separate operation to trace a missing employee of the Jal Shakti department also remained underway.Jammu-Srinagar National Highway (NH-44) remained closed for the second consecutive day Thursday. The 250-km NH, the only all-weather path linking J&K with the rest of India, was blocked at multiple places due to rain-triggered landslides, shooting stones, and road erosion between Jakhani in Udhampur district and Banihal in Ramban district.More than 600 vehicles remained stranded in different stretches of the NH, including Ramban, Nagrota, Jammu, Udhampur, Lakhanpur and Samba, due to the closure. Officials said restoration work was underway, but continuous rainfall was hampering repair and clearance efforts.
